neighbours.label: a share of a whole: the possessive (or the quantifier itself) in 'most of their X', 'a large portion of its X', 'the majority of the X'; a plain possessive without the share stays quiet
fire: Farmers in the region sell most of their crop to a single buyer.
The museum receives a large share of its funding from the state.
Students spend the majority of their day in front of screens.
The airline makes a significant portion of its profit on baggage fees.
Many families lost most of their savings during the crisis.
The charity devotes the bulk of its budget to clean water projects.
The town gets nearly all of its electricity from wind turbines.
Small firms pay a bigger portion of their income in rent.
quiet: Farmers in the region sell their crop to a single buyer.
The museum receives its funding from the state.
Students spend their day in front of screens.
The airline raised its profit by charging baggage fees.
Many families lost their savings during the crisis.
The charity announced its budget for clean water projects.
The town gets its electricity from wind turbines.
Small firms pay their rent at the start of the month.

short: 'most of their' share of a whole
notes: Card: ' their' x6, ' its' x3, ' majority' x2, ' of' x2 after most/portion. Probe: 'a large portion of its revenue' 0.57, 'most of their time' 0.31, 'the majority of the damage' 0.25; 'enjoy their time' 0.01, 'reported its revenue' 0.03. The - pole is the comma before a contrast ('X, instead of Y').
